data.name: Shalmaneser
data.gender_notes: Shalmaneser is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Name of an Assyrian king, derived from shalman, meaning 'god,' and eser, meaning 'righteous.' In the Bible, Shalmaneser is mentioned in 2 Kings 17:30, where he is described as the king of Assyria who carried the Israelites away into captivity. The name Shalmaneser carries the meaning “God of the righteous” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Shalmaneser usually hope their child will grow to embody god of the righteous and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Shalmaneser belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “God of the righteous.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Shalmaneser total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

in_hebrew.name: שלמנאסר
in_hebrew.long_meaning: שלמנאסר הוא שם מלכותי שפירושו 'אל שומר שלום' או 'האל שומר עליו', מורכב מהמילים 'שלום' (שלמ) שפירושו 'שלום' ו'נאסר' (אסר) שפירושו 'אל שומר' או 'אל נצר'. השם מוזכר בתנ'ך כמלך אשור.

in_greek.name: Σαλμανασάρ
in_greek.long_meaning: Ο Σαλμανασάρ είναι ένα βασιλικό όνομα που σημαίνει 'ο Θεός φυλάττει την ειρήνη' ή 'ο Θεός φυλάττει αυτόν', προερχόμενο από τις λέξεις 'Σαλμ' (שלמ) που σημαίνει 'ειρήνη' και 'Νασάρ' (נאסר) που σημαίνει 'ο Θεός φυλάττει' ή 'ο Θεός είναι ο φύλαξ'. Το όνομα αναφέρεται στη Βίβλο ως ένας βασιλιάς της Ασσυρίας.

in_latin.name: Salmaneser
in_latin.long_meaning: Salmaneser est nomen regale quod significat 'Deus custodit pacem' vel 'Deus custodit eum', derivatum ex vocibus 'Salman' (שלמ) quod significat 'pax' et 'Esar' (אסר) quod significat 'Deus custodit' vel 'Deus est custos'. Nomen commemoratur in Scriptura ut rex Assyriae.

in_english.name: Shalmaneser
in_english.meaning: God preserves peace or God keeps him safe
in_english.long_meaning: Shalmaneser is a royal name originating from Hebrew, meaning 'God preserves peace' or 'God keeps him safe'. It is derived from the Hebrew words 'shalom' (peace) and 'nasser' (God preserves or keeps). Shalmaneser is mentioned in the Bible as a king of Assyria, specifically Shalmaneser III, who ruled from 858 to 824 BCE. The name holds significant historical and biblical importance, symbolizing divine protection and peace.

data.cultural_impact: The name Shalmaneser holds significant cultural importance, as it is associated with the powerful Assyrian Empire, which ruled a large portion of the ancient Near East from the late 3rd to the late 1st millennia BCE. King Shalmaneser itself is most notably mentioned in the Bible's Old Testament for leading the Assyrian conquest and exile of the Northern Kingdom of Israel (Samaria) in 722 BCE.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name Shalmaneser lies in the fact that it is derived from shalman, meaning 'god,' and eser, meaning 'righteous.' Thus, even as an Assyrian king of antiquity, Shalmaneser's name epitomizes the belief in divine power and justice. This name underscores the relationship between ancient religious beliefs and the role of a leader in realising divine will and justice within their society.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Shalmaneser is a name of Assyrian origin, meaning "right or just ruler." In the Christian context, it can symbolize the sovereign and just rule of God over His creation. The name carries the Assyrian king's commitment to fairness and justice, reflecting God's perfect and unchanging nature.

biblical_reference.note: Shalmaneser III is mentioned in 2 Kings as a king of Assyria who conquered Israel.

historical_references.context: King of Assyria during the late Bronze Age

It is frequently featured on social media platforms where parents share their naming journeys, and Christian name websites where expectant parents research meaningful Biblical names. The name bridges traditional Christian values with modern faith identity, making it relevant for contemporary families seeking names with deep spiritual and Biblical significance.
